# Fleet Bundle

Generated by AICR v1.0.0

## Prerequisites

- Rancher with Fleet v0.13 or later, where HelmOps are enabled by default
  (tested with Fleet v0.16.1)
- `kubectl` configured for the Rancher management (local) cluster

## Bundles

Fleet reconciles the bundles in this order; each one `dependsOn` the previous
bundle and starts only after it is `Ready`.

| Bundle | Release | Namespace | Version |
|--------|---------|-----------|---------|
| aicr-cert-manager | cert-manager | cert-manager | v1.17.2 |
| aicr-k8s-aibom | k8s-aibom | k8s-aibom-system | 1.5.1 |

## Deployment

1. Apply the HelmOps to the Fleet workspace `fleet-default` on the Rancher
   management cluster. No Git repository is needed: Fleet pulls each chart
   from its repository, with the values inlined in `helmops.yaml`.

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f helmops.yaml
   ```

   `helmops.yaml` is the only file Fleet reads. The `values.yaml` and
   `cluster-values.yaml` files in each folder are kept for reference; edit
   values in `helmops.yaml`, which is also what `aicr bundle --inherit-from`
   and `aicr upgrade-check` read back.

2. Opt clusters in. Nothing is deployed until a cluster carries the label
   the HelmOps select on:

   ```bash
   kubectl label clusters.fleet.cattle.io -n fleet-default <cluster> aicr.nvidia.com/bundle=aicr
   ```

Monitor progress in Rancher under **Continuous Delivery**, or:

```bash
kubectl get bundles -n fleet-default -l aicr.nvidia.com/bundle=aicr
```

If a release with the same name already exists in the target namespace (for
example a GPU Operator installed with `helm install gpu-operator`), Fleet
upgrades it in place. If objects are owned by a release with a different
name, only the first install fails on the ownership conflict; remove or
rename that release first. Once a release exists, every later Fleet deploy is
a Helm upgrade, and Fleet upgrades take ownership of objects owned by other
releases. Removing the HelmOps then deletes those objects too.

## Removal

```bash
kubectl delete -f helmops.yaml
```

Fleet uninstalls every release in the bundle.

## Limitations

- Fleet installs charts with Helm, which creates a chart's `crds/` on first
  install but never upgrades them. These components own
  their CRDs, and the helm deployer refreshes them before every upgrade:

  - k8s-aibom

  Before upgrading any of them, apply the new chart's CRDs with the CRD-apply
  command under "Upgrade, uninstall, and troubleshooting" in the AICR
  component catalog (`docs/user/component-catalog.md`), then let Fleet
  reconcile. Run it against every downstream cluster the bundle targets,
  not the Rancher management cluster: Fleet installs the charts there.
- Readiness hooks (`--readiness-hooks`) are not supported.
- A chart that ships CRDs in `crds/`, templates objects of those kinds, and
  uses Helm `lookup` fails Fleet's server-side dry run on a cluster where the
  CRDs do not exist yet. Apply that chart's CRDs first, to the same clusters.
